description: These yearbooks give the national record of search and rescue operations in Indonesia, an archipelago where ship and aircraft accidents, floods and other disasters make search and rescue a core emergency service. They are published every year by the data and information centre of Basarnas, the National Search and Rescue Agency, under the national One Data programme. Each volume tabulates, for every SAR office, the number of operations in total and by incident type (aircraft accidents, ship accidents, accidents needing special handling, disasters and other conditions endangering people), the numbers of people rescued alive, dead and missing, and the average response time. Further chapters cover preparedness, personnel and community search and rescue capacity, and the agency's facilities, equipment and communication systems. Volumes from 2018 to 2025 are free and available to download as PDF or view as flipbooks. Caveats: tables sit inside PDF books, not data files, the publication states that quoting or reproducing requires the agency's permission, and figures are annual totals per office without incident locations. Simulation uses: setting demand and response time baselines for maritime and disaster search and rescue capacity models, and comparing regional offices. Related records: the Swedish rescue service statistics (data-mcf-sweden-rescue-service-statistics) and the Italian fire corps interventions (data-cnvvf-open-data-interventions) are comparable national sources.
